mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns over 20 days when FEDFUNDS is low, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when UNRATE is below 6%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased demand, leading to higher economic activity and S&P 500 growth.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative despite rising HOUST, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production signals strong supply chains, positively affecting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative S&P 500 returns when INDPRO is above 105 invalidate this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate coupled with rising GDP indicates strong economic growth, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are negative when both FEDFUNDS is low and GDPC1 rises, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Growing employment and retail sales jointly indicate strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative S&P 500 returns despite positive PAYEMS and RSAFS invalidate this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising inflation (CPI) may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive when CPIAUCSL rises, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2% invalidate this hypothesis.
